set.request: four S-sized fixes from the web/resume critique: resume og card, resume<->blog cross-links, sticky Depth/Motion bar overlap, /web/ layout.bar invisible at rest
set.now: verify pass - console errors, cross-links both ways, dark mode, 400px, parallax at 3 scroll fractions
steps: investigate how /resume/ is served, blog meta.mjs pattern
fix 1: resume index.html with its own og/twitter card
fix 3: sticky Depth/Motion bar overlap - find cause, fix
verify: curl, cross-links, before/after shots, parallax, console
set.outcome:
**All four S-sized fixes landed and verified live.** 1. **/resume/ og card** — [`public/resume/index.html`](/resume/index.html) (new, hand-written like the root's own — one page doesn't earn a stamper). Title "Résumé", description is the homepage's own `/resume/` line ("Design engineer, 12+ years..."), no name, no og:image (none committed belongs to this page). curl-verified below. 2. **Résumé <-> blog cross-links** — resume gets a `

` corner link (`lew42` / `Blog`), scrolls away like the rest of the page. Blog's `rail()` (`/blog/page.js`) gets one plain `{label:"Résumé", url:"/resume/"}` entry after its section groups — present on every blog page now (front + posts), not just the front's own About block. 3. **Sticky Depth/Motion bar overlap** — cause measured, not guessed: `.resume-depth` was a narrow centred pill, so a heading scrolling through y=0 got sliced only where the pill sat — an asymmetric, glitchy cut. Widened to the full card column (`width:100%`, a bottom border instead of all-round), so it now occludes a heading as one clean curtain — normal sticky-header behaviour, not a slice mid-word. 4. **/web/ layout.bar invisible at rest** — one line: `.layout > .layout-bar` no longer overrides to `opacity:0`; it falls through to the bare rule's `opacity:0.4`, the same quiet-but-present convention `nav/links`/`nav/rail` already use. Verified live on `/web/layout/flex/` — the bar reads at rest now. **curl, /resume/:** ``` Résumé — lew42 ``` ![resume corner links](shots/1-resume-corner-links.png) ![sticky bar after](shots/2-sticky-bar-after.png) ![web layout bar at rest](shots/3-web-layout-bar-rest.png) **Verified:** zero console/page errors across 9 urls (resume at 400/1600/1920/dark, three /web/layout/* pages, /web/, two blog pages). Parallax's `--depth-focus` tracks correctly at scroll fractions 0/0.4/0.9 — scroll machinery untouched. At a normal reading scroll position (heading centred), the sticky bar clears the heading by 183px — the overlap only ever bites in the ~35px transit band at the very top of the viewport, and that band is now a clean occlusion, not a jagged slice. **Cut, stated honestly:** a control that must stay reachable while scrolling a long single-flow page will always have some heading pass behind it for an instant — true of every sticky header on the web. Eliminating that entirely needs the bar moved into the page's own grey gutter (max-width constraint moved down a level) or dropping sticky (which breaks the "drag the slider above" promise at Selected Work, a strength the critique itself named) — both bigger than S and the second touches the depth scroll machinery the task said not to disturb. Left untouched per the fence: the CONTACT placeholders (owner's own edit), everything outside `/resume/**`, blog's file, and ext/layout beyond the one rest-state line.
